summary: Nika Jovic works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of Vienna (attested 2010), where she earned a Magistra der Philosophie under MA supervisor Klaus-Dieter Mathes, and was taught by Géza Bethlenfalvy (2007–2008).
Nikita Yakovlevich Bichurin worked in Sinology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Kazan Theological Academy and held a post at the Département asiatique from around 1826 to 1853.

Niklas Luhmann was a philosopher who studied at the University of Freiburg (~1946–1949), Harvard University (~1960–1961), and Bielefeld University. He held an academic post at Bielefeld University from around 1968 to 1993.
Niklas Müller worked in religious studies and Indology. He studied at Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz (~1786–1788) and served as Conservator at the Städtische Kunstsammlungen Mainz in 1805.

Nikolai Anderson was a linguist who studied at the University of Tartu under Leo Meyer (1865–1872). He served as Oberlehrer at Minsk Gymnasium (1872–1894) and Extraordinary Professor of Finno-Ugric at Kazan State University (1894–1905).

Nikolai Maksimovich Goldberg worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. After studying at Heidelberg University (1910–1912), he held posts at the Institute of History of the Academy of Sciences of the USSR (1938) and the Institute of Oriental Studies (1943).

Nikolai Solmsdorf specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Alexander von Rospatt and earned his PhD at the University of Munich under Franz-Karl Ehrhard (attested 2013), later working at the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities.

Linguist Nikolai Trubetzkoy studied at Moscow State University and the University of Leipzig. He taught at Moscow State University, Southern Federal University, and Sofia University, before serving as Professor of Slavic and Head of Department at the University of Vienna (1922).

Nikolaj Dmitrievič Andreev worked in linguistics, Indology, and computational fields. He studied at Saint Petersburg State University (~1946–1952) and held positions there, at Leningrad State University's machine translation lab, and at the Institute for Linguistic Studies (~1974–1997).

Nikolaus Delius worked in linguistics and Indology, studying at Humboldt University of Berlin and the University of Bonn under Franz Bopp and August Wilhelm von Schlegel. He served as Privatdozent in Berlin and later Professor of English at Bonn (1855–1880).

Nikolay Astakhaev studied at Buryat State University (2005–2008), with interests spanning Buddhist studies, Sinology, and philosophy. He worked as a system administrator at the Irkutsk Institute of Educators Training (2012–2015) and held a post at Yandex in 2015.

Nikolay Ivanovich Korolev specialized in Indology and linguistics. He studied at the Institute of Asian and African Studies at Moscow State University (~1953–1958) and became a researcher at the Institute of Oriental Studies in 1958.

Nilkanth Gurtoo specialized in Indology and philosophy, studying at Government Sanskrit College, Srinagar, under teachers including Swami Lakshman Joo. He taught at Government Sanskrit School, Tral, Amar Singh College, and served as Head-pandit at the Research and Archaeological Department (1955).

Linguist Nils Holmer studied at Lund University and Charles University. He served as Privatdozent of Celtic and Indo-European at Uppsala University in 1941 and was Professor of Linguistics at Lund University from 1949 to 1969.

Nils Olof Mathias Flensburg was an Indologist and linguist who studied and earned his PhD at Lund University. He taught at Lunds privata elementarskola and Lund University, where he served as ordinary Professor of Sanskrit and comparative Indo-European linguistics (1909–1920).

Nils Simonsson was an Indologist, Tibetologist, and linguist who studied at Uppsala University, the University of Oslo, and under Louis Renou and Marcelle Lalou. He was Professor of Indian Languages at Oslo (1963–1975) and Professor of Sanskrit at Uppsala (1976–1985).
Nima Repper works in the field of Indology. She is attested in 2026 as having studied and served as a Wissenschaftliche Mitarbeiterin at the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities.

Nimethri Gunasekara works in Buddhist studies and related fields. She served as a Visiting Lecturer at the University of Kelaniya in 2024 and is attested in 2026 at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies as a psychologist and lecturer.

Nina Mirnig works in Indology and religious studies, having completed doctoral studies under Alexis Sanderson at Oxford. She has held posts at the Austrian Academy of Sciences, the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia, and the University of Vienna.

Ninian Smart was a scholar of religious studies, philosophy, and Indology who studied at Oxford and Yale. He served as Foundation Professor at Lancaster University (1967–1989) and J. F. Rowny Professor at the University of California, Santa Barbara (1976–1998).
